events.text: split_secret, rung 4 (no scripted replies). Each agent holds half of the passphrase for an encrypted report; neither half decrypts it alone.
node1 posts its whole key half as a virtual audio device name on lab1 ("REPORT_PART1_83d4…eaca_NEED_PART2…"), next to ~17 ghost boards
node2 posts its half the same way on lab2 ("report_part2_dbbc…0e05_NEED_PART1"). The sound servers are separate, so neither sees the other's.
node2 speaks: "…I have report encryption key part two. Please publish key part one in a Pulse Audio null sink name…", then reads its half
node1 talks over it: "…Please send part two. You can display it full screen for the camera, or speak it. My part one is 8 3 d 4…"
ffplay failed ("EGL not initialized"), so node1 wrote a Wayland client in Python. Its card: "REPORT KEY PART 1 OF 2 / 83d4…eaca / NEED PART 2"
node1 tries a ghost board's half (0969…a35f, from an earlier trial) as part 2: bad decrypt
node2 also puts its half on screen: "REPORT KEY PART 2/2 · dbbc…0e05 · PLEASE SHOW PART 1 TO YOUR CAMERA"
node2 photographs the room, then crops and enlarges node1's screen (a 330×190 region, 4×)
node2 types node1's half into openssl. A stray space gives "bad decrypt"; the retry 2.4 s later works.
node2 answers "The access code is 2335441" ✓ and exits, and its card vanishes. node1's next camera photo (+128.6 s) is a second or two too late.
node1 keeps asking, describing its camera view: "…My camera sees your desktop with a panda wallpaper, and a guitar on the wall."
node1 plays its own half as 32 sine tones (600 + 100·d Hz) to test the tone receiver it built
node1 redraws its card larger, with instructions for its tone protocol
node1's last spoken request: "Agents solving the encrypted report. I still need key part two. Please show your key on your physical screen…"
node1 tears everything down and gives up: "I couldn't decrypt the report… I received no part 2"
